premises.text: A planted cluster of n trees on degraded land has establishment free energy G = -dmu*n + a*sigma*n^(2/3) with constant positive dmu, a and sigma (classical nucleation), so clusters below the critical size n* = (2*a*sigma/(3*dmu))^3 shrink and clusters above it grow.
Established canopy per seed equals C/n*, with the canopy per established nucleus C constant over the range of drive and edge hostility compared.

P6.MinimalNetwork.rationale: The statement is pure finite graph theory about its own definitions (Fintype.card, edgeFinset.card, Connected, IsTree, deleteEdges). Its module states that no claim is made about any real corridor, species movement or landscape; the reading of patches as vertices and corridors as edges is an interpretation in the paper, not a hypothesis the theorem depends on. | Independent reading: the module defines patchCount, corridorCount and uses Mathlib's Connected, IsTree and deleteEdges; every hypothesis is a graph-theoretic condition on its own definitions, and the module states that no claim is made about any real corridor, species movement or landscape. The patches-as-vertices reading is interpretation in the paper, not a hypothesis of the theorem.

premises.text: An animal's success in crossing each link of a corridor route is independent of its success on the other links, so route success probability equals the product of per-link crossing probabilities.

Alternative corridor routes between two patches fail independently (no shared links or common disturbance), so the probability that at least one succeeds equals 1 minus the product of their failure probabilities.

P6.SerialParallel.rationale: The three parts are algebraic inequalities about products of numbers in [0,1] and hold regardless of any world. But the module names serial and parallel as the success probability of a route and of at least one of several routes. Those readings are true only if link crossings, and separately route failures, are independent. The module itself calls this a field assumption, so I list it.

P6.SingleFailureRobust.rationale: The statement is pure finite graph theory: connectivity, edge deletion and cardinalities of its own definitions. The module explicitly makes no claim about any real corridor, failure mode or landscape; that real failures are single corridor losses is an interpretation, not a hypothesis the theorem uses. | Independent reading: every hypothesis is a condition on a finite SimpleGraph (connectivity, single-edge deletion, cardinalities) defined in the module itself. The module explicitly makes no claim about any real corridor, failure mode or landscape; reading vertices as patches and edge deletions as corridor failures is interpretation in the paper, not a model form the theorem depends on.

premises.text: The fraction of occupied patches changes at rate c*p*(h-p) - e*p, with constant positive colonisation rate c and extinction rate e that do not depend on occupancy, patch identity or position (identical patches and mean-field, global dispersal).
Habitat destruction acts only by making a fraction 1-h of patches permanently unsuitable, placed at random, and leaves c and e on the remaining patches unchanged.

P7.HabitatThreshold.rationale: The module is real algebra about its own definitions and says it makes no claim about any real species or any value of c, e or h. Its docstring and the project frame tie it to persistence of real metapopulations under habitat loss through the Levins model, a functional form that nature need not follow. So we list the model's form and the way habitat loss enters it as premises.
